items.action: On every `ds-line-chart`, rewrite `yAxisMode="rounded"` to `yAxisMode="aligned"`, `yAxisMode="independent"` to `yAxisMode="dual-grid"` and `yAxisMode="stacked"` to `yAxisMode="split"`. `yAxisMode="exact"` is unchanged. Retype any field, constant or return value that supplies one of those strings.
items.appliesWhen: Only `yAxisMode` on `ds-line-chart`, and any TypeScript typed as `ChartAxisMode` or `LineChartAxisMode` that feeds it. `stack` on `ds-column-chart` keeps its own `"stacked"`, which is a different input with a different meaning and is NOT renamed.
items.pitfall: An unknown string does not error. Angular assigns it, no mode matches, and the plot silently falls back to one shared grid - a chart that still renders and is measured against the wrong axis. A build that passes proves nothing here; only the three old strings being gone does.
items.verify: No `yAxisMode` on a `ds-line-chart` carries `rounded`, `independent` or `stacked`, and every expression bound to `[yAxisMode]` can only produce `aligned`, `exact`, `dual-grid` or `split`.
items.note: The names now say what is done to the gridlines, which is the only thing the four modes differ in. `'stacked'` had to go whatever else happened: `ds-column-chart` ships `stack="stacked"` for SERIES on top of each other, while this mode puts two PLOTS one above the other, and the two charts are read side by side. `'exact'` was the one name that already described itself, so it stays.

Retype any field, constant or return value that supplies one of those strings.
items.appliesWhen: Only `secondaryAxisMode` on `ds-chart`, and any TypeScript typed as `ChartAxisMode` or `LineChartAxisMode` that feeds it. `stack` on `ds-column-chart` keeps its own `"stacked"`, which is a different input with a different meaning and is NOT renamed.
items.pitfall: An unknown string does not error. Angular assigns it, no mode matches, and the plot silently falls back to one shared grid - a chart that still renders and is measured against the wrong axis. A build that passes proves nothing here; only the three old strings being gone does.
items.verify: No `secondaryAxisMode` on a `ds-chart` carries `rounded`, `independent` or `stacked`, and every expression bound to `[secondaryAxisMode]` can only produce `aligned`, `exact`, `dual-grid` or `split`.
items.note: The names now say what is done to the gridlines, which is the only thing the four modes differ in. `'stacked'` had to go whatever else happened: `ds-column-chart` ships `stack="stacked"` for SERIES on top of each other, while this mode puts two PLOTS one above the other, and the two charts are read side by side. The container takes the same four words as the preset, so a combo plot and a line chart are read the same way.

items.action: Only if you SUBCLASS one of these and declare a member of the same name: rename yours, or add `override` where your member genuinely means the same thing.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class extending one of the listed components. Using them in a template is unaffected.
items.pitfall: The collision is a compile error, not a silent one - TS4114 for a same-named member, TS2416 where the signature differs - so a build that passes has none.
items.verify: Every subclass of the listed components builds, and any member it declares that the base now also declares carries `override`.
items.note: `LineChartComponent` gained `curve`, `stack`, `yAxisLabel`, `secondaryAxisLabel` and the members behind them; `ChartComponent` gained `axisLabel`, `secondaryAxisLabel` and the three that thin and turn its category labels; `LineSeriesComponent` gained `curve`. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported, but a release that only adds can still fail such a build on a name collision, which is why the classes are listed here rather than in the additive notes.

items.action: Nothing to write. Where you READ a row's `value` back as a number - summing it, comparing it, passing it on - handle the `[low, high]` pair the type now also allows.
items.appliesWhen: Only code that reads `BarChartRow['value']` back, or declares its own value of that type. Passing a plain number into `data` is unchanged and draws exactly what it did.
items.pitfall: The widening is source-compatible for whoever WRITES the value and breaking for whoever reads it: `total += row.value` is TS2365 now, and a subclass or a mapped type over `BarChartRow` can fail on the invariant position. A chart that only receives data sees nothing at all.
items.verify: Every place that reads a `BarChartRow`'s `value` back narrows it before using it as a number, and the build is clean.
items.note: `value` was `number` and is `number | readonly [low, high]`, so a bar can span between its own ends rather than from zero. The pair is normalised, so either order means the same band.

informational: `ds-line-chart` and `dsLineSeries` take `curve`: `'linear'` (the default, and what every chart already drew), `'step'` or `'smooth'`. Nothing to change - a chart that sets nothing is unchanged. `'smooth'` is a monotone cubic, so it never draws a peak or a trough the readings do not contain.
A filled series now follows its own curve, so the fill and the line share one edge. With the default `'linear'` the drawing is byte-identical to before.

The chart container's marks are published API: `ColumnSeriesComponent`, `LineSeriesComponent`, `ReferenceLineComponent` and `ReferenceLabelComponent`, with `ColumnSeriesPoint`, `LineSeriesData` and `LineSeriesGaps`, now come from the package root as well as from `@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/components/chart`. Purely additive.
A chart tooltip no longer runs off the screen: the panel stops at the viewport height less the overlay's 12px margin and scrolls past that. A panel that already fitted is drawn exactly as before.

A line series measured only against the first axis no longer raises an empty second axis labelled `0`. Affected any plot whose series all read against the left axis; a plot that genuinely carries two scales is unchanged.

`ds-line-chart` takes `stack`: `'none'` (the default, and what every chart already drew), `'stacked'` or `'normalized'`. Nothing to change - a chart that sets nothing is unchanged. Only a series with `area: true` fills, stacking runs per axis, and `stack="stacked"` is not `yAxisMode="split"`: series on top of each other, against two plots one above the other.

`ds-heatmap-chart` is new, from `@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/components/heatmap-chart` and from the package root, with `HeatmapChartRow` and `HeatmapChartCell`. Purely additive - nothing to change. It has no `dataTable` input on purpose: colour is the only channel carrying the quantity on the grid, so the annex table and the colour scale are always drawn.

`ds-waterfall-chart` is new, from `@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/components/waterfall-chart` and from the package root, with `WaterfallChartDatum`, `WaterfallChartKind` and `WaterfallChartStep`. Two tokens come with it, `--ds-chart-positive-color` and `--ds-chart-negative-color`, pointing at the palette's two lead hues rather than at `--success` and `--error`. Purely additive - nothing to change.

A heat scale is new: `--ds-chart-heat-1-color` through `--ds-chart-heat-8-color`, the same hue across the full lightness range for a grid where magnitude is read from the step between two colours. `--ds-chart-ramp-*` is unchanged and `ds-funnel-chart` looks exactly as it did. Purely additive - nothing to change.

`ds-scatter-chart` is new, from `@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/components/scatter-chart` and from the package root, with `ScatterChartSeries`, `ScatterChartDecimator`, `ScatterChartReading` and `ScatterPoint`. Purely additive - nothing to change. It thins its own data past four times the plot's width in marks and says so under the plot; the annex table still lists every reading. `decimator` chooses between the two decimators or turns it off.

A chart's category labels now turn 45 degrees when that lets all of them be drawn, and thin to every second or third only when a tilt is not enough. Nothing to change: it affects what a narrow chart draws, not what a template declares. A chart wide enough for its labels is unchanged.

`ds-line-chart` takes `yAxisLabel` and `secondaryAxisLabel`, and `ds-chart` takes `axisLabel` and `secondaryAxisLabel`, naming what each axis counts. A line chart carrying two scales on one plot also tints each axis with the colour of the series measured against it, derived from the series rather than asked for. Purely additive - a chart with one scale is drawn exactly as before.
